# CUNY Sports Analytics Initiative

### Turn your interest in sports and data into real-world experience.

The **Open Data Lab** is building a student-driven sports analytics initiative focused on using data to support CUNY athletics — and we are looking for CUNY students interested in helping us grow it.

## What Do We Do?

Using our growing **CUNY Sports Database**, students work with real collegiate sports data to create analytics, visualizations, and reports that can provide meaningful insights for CUNY coaches, players, and teams.

Our goal is simple:

> **Help CUNY teams be the best they can be with the help of real data.**

Our current work focuses on **CUNY men's basketball**, where we are developing reproducible scouting and performance reports using historical game and player data.

But basketball is only the beginning.

As the initiative grows, students may help:

- Create scouting reports for men's basketball programs across CUNY
- Analyze team and player performance
- Build data visualizations for coaches and teams
- And so much more!

## Who Are We Looking For?

You **do not need to be an expert** in sports analytics or programming to apply.

If you're a CUNY student interested in **sports, data, programming, visualization, research, or simply learning something new, we want to hear from you!**

Students from **all CUNY colleges and academic backgrounds** are encouraged to apply.

I actually like this **better** than the bullets for a one-pager. The bold terms still make it scannable, but it saves a ton of vertical space.

## What Will You Gain?

This is an opportunity to work on a real, growing analytics project while developing experience in:

**Sports Analytics · R · Data Visualization · SQL · Quarto · Git & GitHub · Reproducible Research · Technical Communication**

You'll also have the opportunity to create **real portfolio work** that demonstrates your skills beyond the classroom.
